summary: Start exclusively assigned round gate agents when their work is ready

replay.detail: No replay trigger or historical rewrite. Gate admission uses existing mission definitions, persisted step states and ordinary intent.desired claims.

schema.detail: No database schema, index, trigger or serialized model change.

rules.detail: No checkpoint rules or digest change.

compatibility.detail: A loop round's step literally named gate defers its exclusively assigned round-local mission declaration until dependencies and baseline predicates pass. Shared seats, pools, root-owned seats and other round declarations remain eager. Subjects, assignments and claim formats are unchanged. Older reconcilers still materialize these seats eagerly. KDL handoffs recognize the parsed deferred declaration; a builder message to that deferred gate satisfies its declaration once durably sent, avoiding a readiness/delivery dependency cycle. Other recipients keep their delivery requirement.

downtime.detail: Requires the ordinary daemon upgrade. Upgrade interruption has not been measured; restart and revision admission are covered by fake-runtime reconciler tests.

manual.detail: No manual migration. Already desired seats are not proactively stopped solely because this build restarts the daemon. Newly materialized rounds use deferred admission; revisions use ordinary generation retirement.

recovery.detail: Daemon restart and compatible revision derive gate admission from durable step state, including a ready gate with no desired seat. Existing claim/release/retry and cleanup paths retain ownership. Returning to an older build restores eager materialization without changing identities or rewriting claims. A selected owned gate declaration also proves prior admission during a pending retry, so a compatible revision re-owns it before predecessor retirement.
